newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Light, gov't to meet on rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Light, gov't to meet on rate hike.

text.p: Rio de Janeiro-based power distributor Light president Michel Gaillard will next week meet government officials to discuss a possible increase in the firm's electricity rates, a company spokesman said.
"We are going to Brasilia next week to discuss this issue with the National Department of Waterway and Eletric Power (DENAE)," said the spokesman, who asked not to be named.
Earlier this year, Mines and Energy Minister Raimundo Brito said the government was not planning any electricity rate increase for 1996 for Brazil's mostly state-owned power sector.
The Light spokesman said that, under a concession contract signed when the firm was privatized in May, the company is allowed to raise rates annually according to an inflation-based formula.

Analysts said Light's rates should be raised by the end of the year because the firm's last adjustment was in November 1995, when the government increased tariffs for all Brazilian electric companies.

By law, the Finance Ministry authorizes public rate adjustments but Light, which is the first major power utility to be privatized, does not need government permission to raise rates, a ministry official said.

"Everything is in (Light's) concession contract and they do not need to report to us. The ministry only controls rate increases of state firms," said the official from the ministry's Price Monitoring Department. Light is controlled by France's ADF and U.S. firms Houston Industries Inc and AES.
